Alignment-only analysis, read-only phase. Requirementsv9, R17 kernels/ABI/n/b/stride unchanged. No numerical run/build during root scoring window.

Actual hardware interface: getconf LEVEL1_DCACHE_LINESIZE=64; sysfs coherency_line_size=64 for all permitted CPUs0..23 L1D, and CPU0 L1/L2/L3 all64. This is observed local hardware, not a hardcoded target assumption.

Actual numerical code: kernels_impl.cpp73-81 madd loops row, then col, then k. It reads b pairs for the dot product, then updates one C element; it does not repeatedly store C in the inner k loop. trsm53-70 copies to private b*b scratch, then writes X row-by-row with an inner triangular read loop. cholesky25-50 writes its diagonal tile and later zeroes its upper triangle.

Actual graph access semantics: madd reads A/B/C and writes C's rectangular tile; the grid builder adds edges only for declared overlapping read/write tiles. At one outer i stage, updates C[k,j] and C[k,j+1] share read-only panel A[k,i] and otherwise disjoint output/read regions (k>=j+1). Neither depends on the other's write, so they can execute concurrently. Example i0,k2,j1: one updates tile(2,1), another(2,2); both depend on completed trsm panels, not each other. No new edge should be added; their physical cache-line overlap is not a logical dependency.

For L base offset s mod line, physical boundary between tile columns is base+8*(row*n+(j+1)*b). If n*8 and b*8 are line multiples and s!=0, last elements of left tile and first elements of right tile share one line for every row, despite distinct matrix elements. Alignment removes that overlap when row/tile byte strides are line multiples. For arbitrary hidden n/b the address remains legal but whole-buffer alignment cannot eliminate every internal boundary; no parameter whitelist or stride padding is justified.

All given public n,b are multiples of8, so local64B alignment would remove that specific output-row boundary overlap. This is static causal evidence only; it does not establish that current vector allocations are actually misaligned or that coherence traffic contributes materially. The current host has no usable PMU in earlier diagnosis. Next authorized diagnostic will sample actual A/L base addresses once per case in a temporary current-main binary, inside scored timer but excluded from scoring conclusions.

Magnitude: an aligned b-element row spans b/8 lines; a nonzero aligned-double offset spans b/8+1. Extra line coverage ratio8/b: b8=100%,b16=50%,b32=25%,b48=16.7%,b64=12.5%,b128=6.25%,b256=3.125%. These are footprint ratios, NOT runtime gains or cache-miss estimates. Same-stage adjacent madd output pairs across all i = q(q-1)(q-2)/6; each pair has b common physical boundary lines if misaligned. q48,b32 gives17296 pairs/553472 pair-row opportunities; q6,b256 only20 pairs/5120 pair-row opportunities. Pair opportunities do not assert temporal overlap.

Expected limits: madd arithmetic/read work scales b^3; boundary interference only touches output edges. q6/b256 critical path is actual kernel CPU, but line-overlap coverage is small and adjacent writers traverse row/col in similar order, so many boundary writes may occur at separated times. Benefits may be stronger for small blocks and write/read boundary interactions. There is no defensible millisecond or score upper bound from these counts; all remaining kernel execute time is the vacuous bound. Do not promise performance.

Minimal potential candidate after actual-pointer evidence: isolated allocation alignment, preferably L-only to test write-sharing, preserving vector capacity/reuse and all existing zeroing/first-touch operations. Derive alignment once from actual permitted CPU cache-line interface (unknown interface falls back to ordinary allocation). Use standards-compliant stateful allocator or equivalent owner with matching allocate/deallocate; no THP advice, no extra threads, no layout/stride changes, no no-init change. Charge alignment extra/padding (at most one line unit for simple over-allocation) in matrix capacity/budget and retained accounting; default allocation fallback must not mis-deallocate. Existing current bulk DeferredZeroAllocator construction semantics, if retained, must stay exactly as baseline comparison. All probe/allocation/free costs remain timed. Test against the exact selected current combination, not obsolete original tree.

Old P008/a3b37ad combined hugepage alignment, uninitialized output storage and MADV_HUGEPAGE, with overlapping noisy full-batch results. That experiment neither proves nor disproves alignment-only. New distinct evidence is the specific adjacent independently scheduled output-tile boundary sharing plus forthcoming actual base address modulo line, not another claim about THP.
